1. There is independent understanding between
the parties on the effect and outcome of what is
stated in paragraph No.’7’ of the order impugned.
2. Advocate S. K. Chaturvedi, appearing for the
respondent, states that the statement recorded in
paragraph ‘7’ is a voluntary step taken by the

--- Page 388 ---
2
respondent to prove the  bona fides and the stay
application is still pending before the High Court.
The High Court will consider the same on merits.
3. Replying to the above argument, Advocate
Bhuwan Raj, argues that the first sentence in
paragraph  ‘7’  records  the  statement  of  the
respondent but the next line is capable of being
understood as granting a stay.
4. We have also read paragraph ‘7’ along with
the learned Advocates appearing for the parties.
5. With a view to give finality to the stay
petition pending, we expunge what has been observed
in paragraph ‘7’ of the impugned order and request
the High Court to dispose of the stay application
moved by the petitioner.
6. The special leave petitions stand disposed
of in the above terms.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand
disposed of.

allegation levelled by the prosecutrix, to the effect that the
appellant subjected her to forcible sexual assault, is totally
false and concocted. In this regard, attention of this Court is
drawn to the testimony of the medical jurist, Dr.Sushma Gond(PW-6),

prolonged period of custody suffered by the appellant, which is
nearly eight years, we are inclined to enlarge the appellant on
bail during the pendency of the instant appeal, by suspending the
sentences awarded to him by the Trial Court and affirmed by the
High Court.
Accordingly, the appellant shall be released on bail upon
furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court and
subject to such other conditions as the Trial Court may deem fit
for releasing the appellant on bail. 
The Trial Court records be summoned, scanned and uploaded.
Soft copies of record be shared with the counsel representing
the parties. 
The appeal be listed for hearing in due course.

1

on record.
The petitioner has been sentenced to fixed term
imprisonment of 10 years. His regular appeal is
pending consideration before the High Court. 
We feel that there is a bleak chance of the
appeal being heard in the near future. The petitioner
has undergone almost 03 years imprisonment as is
evident from the custody certificate. 
In this background, we direct that the sentence
awarded to the petitioner by the Trial Court shall
remain suspended and the petitioner shall be released
on bail during the pendency of appeal before High
Court upon furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction
of  the  Trial  Court  and  subject  to  such  other
conditions as the Trial Court may deem fit for
releasing the appellant on bail.
It goes without saying that the petitioner shall
extend all co-operation in disposal of the appeal. 
The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of in the
above terms. 
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

ITEM NO.101               COURT NO.6               SECTION XIV-A
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Civil Appeal No(s). 3916/2016
THE STATE OF TRIPURA & ORS.                        Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
SMT. SANCHAYEETA DEB                               Respondent(s)
[PART HEARD BY :- HON'BLE DIPANKAR DATTA AND HON'BLE SHEEL NAGU, 
JJ.] 
 
WITH
C.A. No. 12028/2016 (XIV-A)
Date : 19-11-2026 This appeal was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DIPANKAR DATTA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHEEL NAGU
For Appellant(s) : Mr. Shuvodeep Roy- 1672, AOR
                   Mr. Saurabh Tripathi, Adv.
                   Mr. Deepayan Dutta, Adv.
                   Mr. Chirag Kr. Golchha, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) :Ms. Nidhi- 1379, AOR
                   Mr. Dhruv Maheshwari, Adv.
                   Mr. Om Kumar, Adv.
                                      
                   Ms. Asha Gopalan Nair, AOR
                   Ms. Nivedita Nair, Adv.                         
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard Mr. Shuvodeep Roy, learned counsel appearing for the
appellant 1 – State of Tripura.  We have also heard Ms. Asha Gopalan Nair,
learned counsel appearing for the respondent in Civil Appeal No. 3916/2016
(Sanchayeeta Deb) and Ms. Nidhi, learned counsel appearing for respondent in
Civil Appeal No. 12028/2016 (Kanu Chakravarty).
2. Pursuant to the earlier hearing, Mr. Roy has been instructed by the State
to submit that the respective respondents may be reinstated in service but

--- Page 750 ---
2
without back wages.
3. Obviously,  this  suggestion  is  not  acceptable  to  the  respondents.  It  is
contended on their behalf that because of the stigmatic orders of termination
that they suffered, they could not seek further employment.
4. There is no averment on record to the effect that after the termination
orders  were  passed  in  January,  2011,  the  respondents  could  not  secure
employment because of such stigmatic orders. There is also no averment that
the respondents were either unemployed or in some way gainfully employed.
5. We require both the respondents to file their separate affidavits, pleading
therein as to how they survived for all these 15 years post the termination in
January, 2011.
6. It has been submitted by Ms. Nair that the respondent in Civil Appeal No.
3916/2016 (Sanchayeeta Deb) failed to obtain employment as a school teacher
because of the stigma attached to her conduct, as revealed from the impugned
termination order. If indeed that be so, the correspondence that the school and
she exchanged to that effect should also be made part of the affidavit.
7.  The State shall have two weeks’ time to file its reply affidavit and contest
